evidence.note: Title states a specific finding as one declarative sentence with no trailing full stop, as the profile requires.
Insight is plain finding-first prose with evidence ('account for almost all of the network's fall... moved by under 1 point'); no epigram.
Cause-to-consequence explanation in full sentences (staffing shortfall would cut recovery time on every route, so the drop points to the diversion), matching the approved body style.
'The drop is a diversion problem, not a fleet or staffing one' is an 'X, not Y' antithesis the profile bans.
Two-clause 'X, and Y' title ('fell from 86% to 81% in Q3, and retiming ... is the Q4 test'), a construction the profile rejected as AI-sounding; 'is the Q4 test' is framing rather than a finding.
Another 'X, and Y' two-finding title (Mill Street closed in three phases, and routes 12 and 14 ran without retiming).
'Planning and the depot read the same dip differently.' is a mild generic connective line adding no fact.
Driver quote is verbatim under a neutral label with citation, no editorialising.
Three specific, grounded, open questions as the profile asks.

rationale: Titles, Insights, quote tile and prompts mostly follow the profile: specific findings, plain cause-to-consequence prose, verbatim quote. But there are several lapses the presenter would rewrite: an 'X, not Y' antithesis on s-2, 'X, and Y' two-clause titles on s-2 and s-6 (a pattern the profile explicitly rejected), and a filler line on s-7. That fits level 3 rather than 4.
